analysis: Examined LocalTokenizerLoader.swift head lines 73-74, 81 and 104-138. The change adds heldBackBytes, built once at init by probing <0x00>..<0xFF> through convertTokenToId/convertIdToToken round-trips (line 131). Only tokens that round-trip are included, so the unknown-token ID is not misread as a byte. A single-token decode probe (lines 135-137) enables the map only when upstream's ByteFallbackDecoder holds tokens back. decode() (lines 108-122) appends the trailing run of byte tokens that upstream dropped, scanning tokenIds in reverse. When skipSpecialTokens is set, special tokens are skipped. It decodes them with String(decoding:as: UTF8), which turns invalid sequences into U+FFFD rather than trapping. Security relevance: this is output-text fidelity inside the provider process (TB-007, A-001 completions). It does not change encryption, attestation, routing or caching. The decoded text still flows through the existing encrypted response path (T-008 unchanged). The prompt token cache path (lines 35-44, 87-97) and T-041 cache scoping are untouched. Availability: the reverse scan is O(n) per decode, and each skipped special token adds one upstream.decode call. DetokenizerV2 calls decode on bounded segments of about 256 tokens, so no material DoS was identified. That segment bound lives in an unchanged caller that was not supplied. Tokenizer files are operator-controlled (T-012/T-027 pre-existing); a malicious vocabulary can only alter output text, which the operator can already do. The new test file (LocalTokenizerByteFallbackTests.swift, lines 1-170) writes temp directories with UUID names and removes them; it is test-only, with no production surface. No regression identified.
